relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous MEI1 whole-exon deletion in a man with azoospermia (and his sister, who had embryonic arrest) from a consanguineous family, with functional characterization. This directly concerns MEI1-associated spermatogenic failure.

findings.statement: Liu et al. (2025) described a consanguineous family in which a male infertile patient had azoospermia and a female infertile patient had embryonic arrest. Preimplantation genetic testing of the female patient's arrested embryos showed high levels of chromosomal anomalies.
quotes: This study characterized a male infertile patient suffering from azoospermia and a female infertile patient with embryonic arrest from one consanguineous family.
Highly chromosomal anomalies were revealed in arrested embryos with MEI1 mutation.

findings.statement: In the male patient with azoospermia and the female patient with embryonic arrest from a consanguineous family, Liu et al. (2025) used whole-exome sequencing, confirmed by Sanger sequencing, to identify a homozygous deletion of the whole of exon 19 of the MEI1 gene. Amplification and sequencing of cDNA confirmed that the exon was missing, and exon 19 expression was almost undetectable in the patients. Their mother was a heterozygous carrier. In transfected HEK293T cells, the deletion produced a truncated MEI1 protein, consistent with the predicted premature termination in exon 20. The authors stated that this was the first exon rearrangement reported in MEI1.
quotes: The novel homozygous whole exon deletion of exon 19 in MEI1 was detected by WES. Amplification and sequencing of the cDNA verified the deletion of whole exon of MEI1.
Quantitative expression revealed that the deletion result in almost no detectable expression of MEI1 Exon 19 in patients, and their mother is a heterozygous carrier of this whole exon deletion.
Western blotting revealed that the whole exon deletion in MEI1 result in production of truncated MEI1 protein, corresponding to the predicted premature termination at Exon 20 of MEI1.

variants.as_reported: homozygous whole exon deletion of exon 19 in MEI1

relevance_reason: Reports bi-allelic MEI1 variants in four Chinese men with non-obstructive azoospermia and meiotic arrest, which defines this spermatogenic failure entry.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2023) described 4 Chinese men with non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA). Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining showed that spermatogenesis was arrested at the spermatocyte stage. The patients also had defective homeostasis of programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and defective meiotic chromosome synapsis.
quotes: bi-allelic deleterious variants in meiosis inhibitor protein 1 (MEI1) were identified by whole-exome sequencing in four Chinese patients with NOA

Testicular pathologic analysis and immunohistochemical staining revealed that spermatogenesis is arrested at spermatocyte stage, with defective programmed DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) homoeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis in patients carrying the variants.

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing, Zhang et al. (2023) identified bi-allelic deleterious variants in the MEI1 gene in 4 Chinese patients with non-obstructive azoospermia and meiotic arrest. The authors concluded that bi-allelic MEI1 variants could cause defective DSB homeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis, which lead to meiotic arrest and male infertility.
quotes: bi-allelic deleterious variants in meiosis inhibitor protein 1 (MEI1) were identified by whole-exome sequencing in four Chinese patients with NOA

our findings provide direct genetic and functional evidences that bi-allelic variants in MEI1 could cause defective DSBs homoeostasis and meiotic chromosome synapsis, which subsequently lead to meiosis arrest and male infertility.

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2023) found a missense variant in MEI1, c.G186C, as one of the bi-allelic variants in their patients with NOA. In vitro, this variant reduced MEI1 expression.
quotes: one missense variant (c.G186C) reduced the expression of MEI1

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2023) found a frameshift variant in MEI1, c.251delT, in their patients with NOA. In vitro, this variant led to truncated MEI1 proteins.
quotes: one frameshift variant (c.251delT) led to truncated proteins of MEI1 in in vitro

findings.statement: Zhang et al. (2023) found a missense variant in MEI1, c.T1585A, in their patients with NOA. Based on bioinformatic analysis, the authors assumed that this variant affects the interaction between MEI1 and its partners.
quotes: the missense variant (c.T1585A) was assumed to affect the interaction between MEI1 and its partners via bioinformatic analysis

relevance_reason: Reports two brothers with cryptozoospermia/spermatogenic failure carrying compound heterozygous MEI1 variants inherited from heterozygous parents.

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2023) reported 2 Chinese brothers with infertility due to cryptozoospermia. The proband, a 30-year-old man with 5 years of infertility, had normal external genitalia, bilateral testicular volumes of about 12 ml, and normal semen volume and pH; no sperm were seen in the initial semen smear, but centrifuged sediment showed 0-1 sperm per high-power field (10-15 sperm in 20 HPF), few of them motile. Serum FSH, LH, testosterone, estradiol, prolactin, inhibin B, and AMH were normal, the karyotype was 46,XY, and there were no Y-chromosome AZF microdeletions. His brother had 3 years of infertility and also had cryptozoospermia, with normal physical examination, hormones, karyotype, and Y-microdeletion testing.
quotes: Semen centrifugal sediment smear showed that the sperm count was 0–1 cells per high-power field (HPF) revealing cryptozoospermia.

He was 178 cm tall and weighted 77 kg, with normal external genital development, bilateral testicular volumes of approximately 12 ml, and no palpable abnormalities found in the bilateral spermatic cord and vas deferens.

Several semen tests indicated that no sperm could be found in his initial semen smear, but 0–1 motile sperm were occasionally seen after the semen centrifugation smear, also revealing cryptozoospermia.

findings.statement: In 2 Chinese brothers with cryptozoospermia, Chen et al. (2023) identified compound heterozygous variants in the MEI1 gene: a c.529+5G>A splice site variant downstream of exon 5 (predicted to affect splicing) and a c.2071C>G transversion in exon 18 resulting in a gln691-to-glu (Q691E) substitution. The variants, found by whole-exome sequencing and confirmed by Sanger sequencing, were absent from ExAC and gnomAD. The father was heterozygous for the missense variant and the mother for the splice variant; the father had normal fertility. Testicular tissue and sperm were not available for functional study.
quotes: A novel compound heterozygous mutation was identified in the meiotic double-stranded break formation protein 1 (MEI1) gene (Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man [OMIM]: 608797), including the missense mutation c.2071C>G (p.Gln691Glu) located in exon 18 and the splicing mutation c.529+5G>A located downstream of exon 5.
These two variants have not been included in ExAC or gnomAD thus far.
The father (II:2) of the brothers was a c.2071C>G heterozygous carrier, while their mother (II:3) was a c.529+5G>A heterozygous carrier (Figure 1).

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2023) suggested that the combination of the two MEI1 variants may permit slight MEI1 expression, sometimes allowing meiosis to occur and resulting in cryptozoospermia rather than nonobstructive azoospermia.
quotes: We can suggest that the combination of the two heterozygous variants may cause slight expression of MEI1 and thus sometimes allow meiosis to occur, resulting in cryptozoospermia rather than NOA.

findings.statement: Chen et al. (2023) stated that the MEI1 variants in the affected brothers were inherited from parents who were each heterozygous carriers, indicating autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: The mutations were inherited from their parents, who were both single heterozygous carriers, indicating a recessive pattern of inheritance.

relevance_reason: This whole-genome sequencing study of 39 men with nonobstructive azoospermia reports candidate variants in several genes, including TKTL1, IGSF1, ZFPM2, VCX3A and ESX1. It does not test segregation. The functional work is limited to structural modeling and, for TKTL1 only, expression studies. Which of these genes is the subject of SPGF103 cannot be told from the header, so the paper is classed as supporting evidence.

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) performed whole-genome sequencing in 39 men with nonobstructive azoospermia (NOA). Six of them had previously had uninformative whole-exome sequencing. All 39 had a normal karyotype and no Y chromosome microdeletions or CFTR mutations. Using a recessive model (hemizygous, homozygous or compound heterozygous) and filtering at gnomAD VAF < 0.01, the authors identified candidate NOA-associated variants in 29 of the 39 men, and in 5 of the 6 men with prior negative exome sequencing.
quotes: In this study, we identified novel potential candidate NOA-associated genes in 29 individuals out of 39 azoospermic males.
Note that in 5 out of 6 patients subjected previously to WES analysis, which did not disclose potentially causative variants, the WGS analysis was successful with NOA-associated gene findings.

All the patients were tested and did not show the following causes of infertility: abnormal karyotype, Y chromosome microdeletions, CFTR gene mutations, presence of antisperm antibodies, active or past orchitis, testicular torsion, cryptorchidism or varicocele.

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) classified the testicular biopsies of the NOA patients by histopathology and Johnsen score: 16 showed postmeiotic arrest (Johnsen 6-9), 3 meiotic arrest (Johnsen 4-5), 3 premeiotic arrest (Johnsen 3), and 10 Sertoli cell-only syndrome (Johnsen 2).
quotes: Testicular samples were classified into four categories by histopathological image description: postmeiotic arrest (Johnsen score 6–9: 16 samples), meiotic arrest (Johnsen score 4–5: 3 samples), premeiotic arrest (Johnsen score 3: 3 samples), and Sertoli‐cell‐only syndrome (SCOS; Johnsen score 2: 10 samples)

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) identified 2 ultrarare variants in the X-linked TKTL1 gene (Xq28) in 2 men with NOA, both predicted to be disease causing. One was c.268_268delG (p.Asp90Metfs*35), found in a patient with meiotic arrest; the other was c.1601A>G (p.Glu534Gly), located in the C-terminal domain. Neither variant was found in gnomAD. Neither patient showed TKTL1 expression at the mRNA or protein level. Structural modeling suggested that the Glu534Gly change destabilizes the fold of the C-terminal domain, which helps mediate homodimerization.
quotes: We identified two ultrarare variants (c.268_268delG and c.1601A>G) in the TKTL1 gene (locus Xq28), and in silico analysis showed a disease‐causing effect in MutationT@ster (Table 1).
The c.268_268delG variant was detected in patient with MA arrest and led to the following change in the protein: p.Asp90Met fs*35
For both patients, we observed lack of expression of the TKTL1 gene at both mRNA and protein levels (Figure S2C,D).

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) identified 4 hemizygous variants in the X-linked IGSF1 gene (Xq26.1) in 4 of 39 men with NOA. These were c.758A>G (p.Tyr253Cys) in patient P31L, who had Sertoli cell-only syndrome; c.1184T>G (p.Leu395Arg) in P10L, who had postmeiotic arrest; c.2554T>G (p.Tyr838Asp) in P45L, who had postmeiotic arrest; and the intronic variant g.114567C>G in P41P, who had meiotic arrest. Three of the 4 variants had not been reported in ClinVar; c.1184T>G was listed there as benign. Homology modeling suggested that Leu395Arg would deform the Ig domain fold.
quotes: We also identified four likely pathogenic variants in the IGSF1 gene (c.758A>G, c.1184T>G, g.114567C>G, c.2554T>G) (locus Xq26.1) in 4 out of 39 patients.

Variant c.758A>G was identified in patient P31L with SCOS and led to an amino acid change (p.Tyr253Cys) in the third C2‐type Ig loop, whereas variant c.1184T>G was observed in a patient with postmeiotic arrest (P10L) and introduced an amino acid change (p.Leu395Arg) in the fourth C2‐type Ig loop
Three out of four variants in the IGSF1 sequence have not been previously reported in the ClinVar database. Only c.1184T>G variant was reported as benign but lacked a detailed phenotypic description.

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) identified compound heterozygous ZFPM2 variants, c.89A>G (p.Glu30Gly) and c.2287G>A (p.Val763Ile), in patient P10L, who had NOA with postmeiotic arrest. The c.2287G>A (p.Val763Ile) variant was also found in the homozygous state in a second patient with postmeiotic arrest (P9L). All of these variants were predicted in silico to be disease causing. The authors noted that c.89A>G had previously been associated with 46,XY sex reversal-3.
quotes: In our experiments, we identified the following variants of the ZFPM2 gene in azoospermic patient P10L with postmeiotic arrest: compound heterozygous variants c.89A>G and c.2287G>A, which introduced amino acid change p.Glu30Gly and p.Val763Ile, respectively (Table 1, Figure 1C).
One of these variants (c.2287G>A; p.Val763Ile) was also observed in another patient with postmeiotic arrest (P9L) as a homozygous variant (Table 1).

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) identified an ultrarare hemizygous VCX3A variant, c.556G>A (p.Val186Met), in a man with NOA and Sertoli cell-only syndrome. VCX3A is located at Xp22.31 and is expressed only in the testis.
quotes: Moreover, we identified the ultrarare variant c.556G>A within the VCX3A gene (locus Xp22.31) in a patient with SCOS (Table 1), which is expressed exclusively in the testis
This variant c.556G>A introduced the amino acid change p.Val186Met (Table 1, Figure 1D).

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) found biallelic rare variants in autosomal genes previously linked to infertility in individual NOA patients. These were TEX14 c.2285_2288delAGAA (homozygous); and compound heterozygous variants in DNAH1 (c.8455G>A, c.11494_11495delinsAG), FANCM (g.19521G>A, c.2081T>G), FSIP2, PMFBP1, MEI1 (c.1546A>G, c.3542G>A), PIWIL1 and WDR66. A homozygous QRICH2 variant was also found.
quotes: This group included new variants in known genes related to somatic chromosomes associated with infertility such as TEX14 (locus 17q22; c.2285_2288delAGAA: homozygous), DNAH1 (locus 3p21.1; c.8455G>A, c.11494_11495delinsAG: compound heterozygous), FANCM (locus 14q21.2; g.19521G>A, c.2081T>G: compound heterozygous)
MEI1 (locus 22q13.2; c.1546A>G, c.3542G>A: compound heterozygous)

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) found ultrarare ESX1 variants (c.1040C>G, c.1042C>G) and a TEX13A variant (c.596G>A) in NOA patients with postmeiotic arrest. The authors noted that the ESX1 variants resemble variants previously reported in Han Chinese men with NOA (c.1094C>G, c.1096C>G). They predicted that the ESX1 variants would destabilize cyclins.
quotes: In particular, we noted ultrarare variants of the ESX1 gene (c.1040C>G, c.1042C>G) and TEX13A (c.596G>A) that were detected in patients with postmeiotic arrest (Table 2).

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) also found rare hemizygous variants in X-linked genes previously implicated in infertility. These included KCND1 c.1723T>G, KIAA1210 c.1214G>A, FAM47C c.1826A>G, ZMYM3 c.2367C>G and FANCB c.1769T>C. They also found a homozygous FAM50B variant, c.293G>A, in patient P9L, who had postmeiotic arrest.
quotes: In particular, the following variants should be highlighted: c.1723T>G in the KCND1 gene (locus Xp11.23), c.1214G>A in the KIAA1210 gene (locus Xq24), and c.1826A>G in the FAM47C gene (locus Xp21.1).
FAM50B (locus 6p.25.2), which was identified in a patient with postmeiotic arrest (P9L) following homozygous variant c.293G>A

findings.statement: Malcher et al. (2022) observed marked genetic heterogeneity among the NOA patients: of the 29 men with candidate variants, only 2 (in one case 3) shared the same variant. Sixteen of the 58 rare variants had not been reported before.
quotes: We noted that among identified variants only two (in one case 3) of the 29 individuals shared the same variant—overlaps (Table S2). The 16 out of the 58 rare variants were totally newly discovered SNVs

relevance_reason: The abstract reports biallelic mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114 in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles, plus a Mei1-deficient female mouse model. It does not describe male spermatogenic failure, so it only gives context on the genes involved.

findings.statement: Nguyen et al. (2018) identified biallelic deleterious mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114 in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles. These genes have roles in forming meiotic double-strand breaks.
quotes: We identified bi-allelic deleterious mutations in MEI1, TOP6BL/C11orf80, and REC114, with roles in meiotic double-strand breaks formation in women with recurrent androgenetic complete hydatidiform moles.

findings.statement: Nguyen et al. (2018) found that 8% of oocytes from Mei1-deficient female mice lost all their chromosomes by extruding them, together with the spindles, into the first polar body. Mei1-/- oocytes could be fertilized, and 5% produced androgenetic zygotes. The authors proposed that extrusion of all maternal chromosomes is a mechanism for producing androgenetic zygotes.
quotes: We investigated the occurrence of androgenesis in Mei1-deficient female mice and discovered that 8% of their oocytes lose all their chromosomes by extruding them with the spindles into the first polar body.
We demonstrate that Mei1-/- oocytes are capable of fertilization and 5% produce androgenetic zygotes.
